counterfactual_missing_items: Pancreatic tissue biopsy confirming adenocarcinoma was not performed
No abdominal tenderness or acute peritoneal signs were present
No jaundice or scleral icterus was noted
decisive_items: Cutaneous lesion biopsy: 'Ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification
painful nodules on the anterior shins and inner left thigh
1.9 × 1.7-cm mass in portal vein with extension to superior mesenteric vein
response.rationale: R2 integrates the pathognomonic ghost-cell fat necrosis on skin biopsy, subcutaneous nodules, marked lipase/amylase elevation, and pancreatic head mass with vascular extension, fitting pancreatic cancer with panniculitis. R4 relies only on enzyme elevation and pancreatic cystic lesions, ignoring the panniculitis and malignancy features.

rejected.why: Necrotizing pancreatitis does not explain the chronic painful nodules, ghost-cell fat necrosis on biopsy, polyarthralgia, or portal vein mass/CA 19-9 elevation; absence of abdominal tenderness also argues against it.
